title: ITD 140 Quiz 1 Study Guide
description: AI and machine learning, the three types of learning, classification and regression, k-means, parameters and hyperparameters, accuracy and the confusion matrix, generalization, and the machine learning process, in the same order as the quiz and flashcards.

blocks.text: Two different words

rows: The overall field or science of making machines perform tasks that need intelligence
One specific approach to AI: the system **learns rules from data** instead of being given them

blocks.text: Machine learning is a **subset** of AI. A program of hand-written if/else rules can be AI, but it is not ML, because nothing is learned.
Vocabulary

rows: The examples the algorithm learns from
What the training algorithm produces; used to make predictions
The value the model is trained to **predict**

blocks.label: Remember:
blocks.text: AI is the whole field; ML is one approach inside it. Not every AI system uses ML.

rows: Emails already marked spam or not spam
**No labels**; the algorithm finds structure itself
A program learning a game by its score

blocks.label: Remember:
blocks.text: Ask what the data comes with. Labels means supervised, nothing means unsupervised, and a reward from the environment means reinforcement.
Both are **supervised** learning. What separates them is the target variable.

rows: Dog or not dog; spam or not spam
kNN, decision tree, random forest, neural net, logistic regression

blocks.label: Watch out:
blocks.text: **Logistic regression** has 'regression' in its name but is almost always used for **binary classification**. Linear regression is the one that predicts continuous numbers.
**kNN** classifies a new example by the labels of its k closest training examples.
**Clustering** groups unlabelled examples so that similar ones end up together. It is **unsupervised** learning.
k-means

items: The hyperparameter **k** is the **number of clusters** you want the algorithm to find.
It starts with **random positions** for each **centroid** (the centre of a cluster).
It then repeats: assign each point to its nearest centroid, and move each centroid to the centre of its points, until they settle on the actual cluster centres.

blocks.label: Remember:
blocks.text: Because the starting centroids are random, two runs can give different clusters. And k in k-means (clusters) is not the same as k in kNN (neighbours).

rows: The training algorithm, while it learns
Centroid positions; the slope a regression learns
k in k-means; neighbours in kNN

blocks.label: Remember:
blocks.text: Parameters are trained. Hyperparameters are chosen.
accuracy = number correct / total number of samples
45 correct out of 60 samples gives 45 / 60 = **75%**. If you are told the number **wrong**, subtract first: 18 wrong out of 200 means 182 correct, so 91%.
Confusion matrix
A grid comparing **actual** classes with **predicted** classes. Correct predictions sit on the **diagonal**; every other cell is a mistake, and shows which classes get confused with which.
Accuracy here is (40 + 45) / 100 = **85%**. The 10 is cats the model called dogs.
**Generalization** is how well a model works on **unseen** examples, those not in its training set. Training accuracy comes from the training data; **test accuracy** comes from data held back.

rows: Too simple to capture the complexity of the data

items: High training accuracy, low test accuracy: **overfit**, variance too high.
Low training accuracy: **underfit**, bias too high.

blocks.label: Watch out:
blocks.text: High training accuracy proves nothing about new data. Always check the test accuracy.
A common short-answer question asks for the **basic steps to train and check a model**. Learn the steps in order, and learn how they group into **three main points**.

rows: Collect the examples (rows) the model will learn from
Pick the input variables (features) and the one variable to predict (target / label)
Divide into a **training set** and a **test set** so some examples stay unseen
Choose an algorithm and its hyperparameters; the algorithm learns the **parameters** from the training set
Measure accuracy on the **test set** and compare it with training accuracy

blocks.text: The same process as three points

items: **Prepare the data:** gather it, identify features and target, split into training and test sets.
**Train the model:** fit it to the training set.
**Evaluate the model:** test it on the test set and check accuracy and generalization.

blocks.label: Remember:
blocks.text: The test set is **never** used for training. Steps 2 and 3 can swap places (the split does not depend on which columns are features). If the test result is poor, adjust (different algorithm or hyperparameters, more data) and repeat from step 4.
This order is a reasonable summary of the topic list, not a confirmed marking scheme. If your instructor's wording differs, use theirs.
